name: Key Steps for Transforming Below-Grade Rooms with Basement Interior Finishing

step.name: Step 1: Foundation inspection and moisture diagnostic phase
step.text: Examine all exterior-facing concrete walls and slab sections for dampness, white mineral deposits, or settling cracks. Make any required exterior drainage adjustments or interior water repairs so surfaces are dry before construction starts.

step.name: Step 2: Interior framing and soffit construction phase
step.text: Snap layout lines and construct perimeter walls with a proper thermal gap from the concrete. Frame around overhead duct trunks, support beams, and structural teleposts while building accessible frames for utility equipment.

step.name: Step 3: Trade rough-in and ventilation installation phase
step.text: Coordinate licensed sub-trades to run electrical circuits, plumbing supply and waste lines, and HVAC extensions through the framed cavities. Install dedicated exhaust ducting for any below-grade bathrooms directly to the home exterior.

step.name: Step 4: Municipal inspection and insulation placement phase
step.text: Walk the framed space with city building inspectors to secure sign-offs on structural, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical rough work. Once approved, install approved below-grade insulation products to create a continuous thermal barrier.

step.name: Step 5: Drywall, interior trim, and surface finishing phase
step.text: Hang, tape, and sand drywall before applying primer and durable interior paint. Lay moisture-tolerant flooring, install interior doors, mount trim molding, and attach plumbing and lighting fixtures to complete the room.
